title: Participle Clauses
grammar_goal: Demonstrates advanced Grammatical Range (Band 7-9) by concisely giving reasons, results, or conditions without using full standard clauses.

core_rule.formula: Present Participle (V-ing) / Past Participle (V-ed/3) / Perfect Participle (Having + V3) + main clause
core_rule.usage: Use V-ing for active meanings or things happening at the same time. Use V-ed for passive meanings or conditions. Use Having + V3 for an action completed before the main action. The subject of the participle clause must be the same as the subject of the main clause.

when_to_use: Task 2: To give reasons elegantly (e.g., 'Realising the danger, the government acted...').
Task 1 (Maps): To describe locations passively (e.g., 'Located in the north, the forest...').
Task 1 (Processes): To describe sequential steps (e.g., 'Having been cleaned, the bottles are...').
when_not_to_use: Do not use if the subjects of the two clauses are different (this creates a 'dangling modifier' e.g., 'Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful' implies the trees were walking).
Avoid overusing them in Speaking Part 1; they are very formal and better suited for written or highly academic contexts.

ielts_examples.writing: Having analyzed the data thoroughly, the researchers concluded that immediate action was necessary.
ielts_examples.speaking: Growing up in a rural area, I learned to appreciate the quietness of nature.

repair_section.wrong: Because he was tired, he went to bed early.
repair_section.correct: Being tired, he went to bed early.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: Exhausted from the day's labor, he retired for the evening prematurely.

repair_section.wrong: Looking out the window, the sun was shining.
repair_section.correct: Looking out the window, I saw the sun shining.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: Gazing through the window, I observed the radiant sunlight.

repair_section.wrong: After they finished the test, the students left.
repair_section.correct: Having finished the test, the students left.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: Having completed the examination, the candidates exited the hall.

vietnamese_learner_mistakes: Dangling Modifiers: The subject of the main clause doesn't match the implied subject of the participle clause.
Using V-ing when a passive V-ed meaning is needed (e.g., 'Building in 1990, the house...' instead of 'Built in 1990...').
Forgetting the comma after an introductory participle clause.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: Driving to work, a dog ran across the road.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: Driving to work, I saw a dog run across the road.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: Because it was built of wood, the house caught fire easily.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: Built of wood, the house caught fire easily.

image_prompt_fallback: A sleek, minimalist arrow combining two elements into one, representing the concise nature of participle clauses.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses a perfect participle clause?

options.A: Having read the book, the movie was a disappointment.
options.B: Having read the book, I found the movie disappointing.
options.C: Have reading the book, I found the movie disappointing.
options.D: Read the book, I found the movie disappointing.

quiz.explanation: Option B is correct. 'Having read' shows the action finished before the main clause. The subject 'I' correctly matches who read the book. Option A is a dangling modifier.
